newsitem.title: UK: Exco warns on profits, restructuring charge.
newsitem.headline: Exco warns on profits, restructuring charge.

text.p: Wholesale securities broking group Exco Plc on Friday reiterated its cautious outlook for the first half and said that pre-tax profits were likely to be around 7 million stg.
The figures would also include a net restructuring provison of 2 million stg to cover the costs of 154 redundancies since the start of the year.
The strength of sterling has reduced profits by some two million stg in the first six months of 1997.
The interim dividend is to be halved to 0.75 pence per share and unless trading improves markedly in the second half a similar cut in the full year dividend was likely, Exco said.

In the 1996 accounts, Exco said its strategy was to focus on securities, derivatives, capital markets and interest rate products where opportunities for profitable growth existed and withdraw from areas where there was overcapacity and margins were thin.
In New York, securities broking and moneybroking, previously two separate offices, are to be relocated to a new site and integrated into a single operation.
The move will mean immediate savings of 1.5 million stg annually and new technology will produce another one million stg in operating efficiencies.
A 6.2 million stg provision will be made in the second half for the surrender of the leases of the existing premises and write-off of fixed assets.
A reorganisation and re-equipment programme in London will result in a further one million stg provision in the second half.
